item.content:encoded:
Bayside Academy's football team picked up a statement win Thursday night, defeating the Jackson Aggies 29-18 in what amounted to a marquee matchup for the second week of the season.

Despite Jackson entering the game with an extra contest already on their schedule, the Admirals proved their mettle with a dominant defensive performance that held the Aggies well below 20 points. The win signals early momentum for Bayside as the squad continues building chemistry under its offense and defense.

The game drew attention across the region as one of Week 2's most significant contests, according to WKRG News 5. Both teams looked to establish themselves early in what shapes up to be a competitive season ahead.

item.title: Prichard mayor's self-insurance claim questioned in investigation
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: An investigation by WKRG News 5 suggests the City of Prichard may not actually be self-insured, contradicting claims made by Mayor Carletta Davis following the city's loss of municipal insurance coverage on August 1. After the insurance lapsed, Davis sent a letter to city employees indicating they would be covered under a self-insurance…
item.content:encoded:
An investigation by WKRG News 5 suggests the City of Prichard may not actually be self-insured, contradicting claims made by Mayor Carletta Davis following the city's loss of municipal insurance coverage on August 1.

After the insurance lapsed, Davis sent a letter to city employees indicating they would be covered under a self-insurance arrangement temporarily. However, the news investigation raised questions about whether Prichard actually has the financial capacity or legal standing to operate under such a plan.

The findings raise concerns about potential liability exposure for city employees and residents during any period without traditional municipal coverage. Self-insurance typically requires significant financial reserves and regulatory approval, neither of which appear to be clearly documented in Prichard's case, according to the WKRG report.

The investigation comes as Prichard continues to face ongoing financial challenges that have plagued the municipality for years. The city has not yet responded publicly to the specific findings about its insurance status.

item.content:encoded:
The Mobile Parks and Recreation Department is rolling out ACT preparation workshops to help students gear up for the standardized test. According to WKRG News 5, the department is offering two workshops across three separate months to give students flexibility in their schedules.

The workshops are designed to help students understand the test format, review key concepts, and develop test-taking strategies before sitting for the actual ACT. While details on specific dates and registration weren't immediately available, students interested in participating should contact the Mobile Parks and Recreation Department directly for more information about availability and enrollment.

ACT scores play a significant role in college admissions and scholarship decisions, making test preparation an important step for high school students planning their post-secondary futures.

item.title: Fort Morgan Trail expansion opens 4 miles of new pathways
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A freshly completed section of the Fort Morgan Trail in Alabama is now open to the public, giving visitors more than four miles of additional pathways to explore along the historic fort's grounds. Alabama State Parks marked the occasion with a ribbon-cutting ceremony Friday, extending recreational opportunities for hikers and nature enthusiasts…
item.content:encoded:
A freshly completed section of the Fort Morgan Trail in Alabama is now open to the public, giving visitors more than four miles of additional pathways to explore along the historic fort's grounds. Alabama State Parks marked the occasion with a ribbon-cutting ceremony Friday, extending recreational opportunities for hikers and nature enthusiasts visiting the coastal landmark.

The trail expansion adds to the existing network at Fort Morgan State Historic Site, which sits at the tip of a narrow peninsula jutting into Mobile Bay. The addition gives visitors more scenic routes through the area while maintaining access to the fort's historical structures and waterfront views.

Fort Morgan has long been a popular destination for both history buffs interested in the Civil War-era fortress and outdoor recreation seekers looking to enjoy Alabama's Gulf Coast. The expanded trail system aims to enhance that appeal by offering more opportunities to experience the natural landscape surrounding the historic site.

The park on Gulf Beach Highway has new playground equipment, ADA-accessible amenities and new fencing. item.content:encoded: Escambia County will hold a grand reopening and ribbon-cutting next Thursday, Sep. 3 at 10 a.m. for the newly improved Perdido Kids Park. The park on Gulf Beach Highway has new playground equipment, ADA-accessible amenities and new fencing. County officials say several longtime features were preserved, including the children’s handprint wall, climbing trees, airplane rocker toys, swings and picnic pavilion. District Two Commissioner Mike Kohler says the park is important to the community and he’s looking forward to seeing families return. The reopening will be held at the park at 10004 Gulf Beach Highway.

item.title: Mobile County Schools celebrates surge in AP test success
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: Mobile County Public Schools is recognizing nearly 400 students who earned qualifying scores on Advanced Placement exams this year, marking a significant milestone for the district. According to school officials, the number represents a more than 25% increase compared to last year's cohort of successful test-takers. The jump in AP participation…
item.content:encoded:
Mobile County Public Schools is recognizing nearly 400 students who earned qualifying scores on Advanced Placement exams this year, marking a significant milestone for the district. According to school officials, the number represents a more than 25% increase compared to last year's cohort of successful test-takers.

The jump in AP participation and success reflects growing student interest in college-level coursework during high school. AP courses and exams allow students to earn college credit while still in secondary school, potentially saving time and money on their post-secondary education.

School leaders attribute the increase to expanded access to AP programs and increased student engagement across Mobile County schools. The district is honoring these students for their academic achievement and commitment to challenging coursework.

item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Transportation is warning drivers in Okaloosa County to expect a temporary traffic shift on U.S. 98 at Brooks Bridge starting this weekend.

According to FDOT, the traffic adjustment is scheduled to begin the week of Sunday, Aug. 30. The agency hasn't released specifics on the duration or exact nature of the shift, but drivers heading through the area should plan for potential delays or lane changes.

U.S. 98 is a major east-west corridor through the panhandle, and Brooks Bridge carries significant traffic volume. FDOT recommends drivers monitor local traffic updates and allow extra travel time during the work period.

Residents who use storage facilities in Santa Rosa County are urged to verify their units remain secure and report any suspicious activity to local police.

item.content:encoded:
A vehicle crashed through the front of a retail store in Mobile Thursday afternoon, causing damage to multiple businesses in the area, according to Mobile Police Department.

The incident occurred when a car drove through the storefront of one of the shops. Both a Cato and Hibbett Sports location sustained damage from the crash.

Mobile police responded to the scene and are investigating the circumstances surrounding the collision. Details about injuries, the cause of the crash, and the extent of damage to both stores were not immediately available.

The investigation remains ongoing as authorities work to determine how the vehicle ended up crashing through the storefront.

item.content:encoded:
The Niceville Fire Department has sent one engine and a Battalion Chief to Texas to assist in battling large-scale wildfires, according to department officials.

The deployment is part of regional mutual aid efforts to support firefighting operations in Texas. Officials emphasized that the move will not affect service levels for Niceville residents, as the department maintains adequate resources to handle local emergency response.

This type of cross-state assistance is common during major fire seasons, allowing departments across the country to share personnel and equipment to combat large wildfires that can quickly overwhelm local resources.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola's iconic Graffiti Bridge has been transformed into a tribute to country music legend Dolly Parton following her recent death. The mural joins countless other memorials being created around the world as fans and artists grapple with the loss of the legendary performer, according to WKRG News 5.

The Graffiti Bridge, a beloved local landmark known for its ever-changing street art, has become a gathering place for community expression and remembrance. The Dolly Parton mural represents one of the latest additions to the bridge's ongoing artistic canvas, where residents and visitors have long left their marks.

Parton's influence on music and popular culture spanned decades, and her passing prompted an outpouring of tributes from fans worldwide. Pensacola's artistic community chose to honor her legacy through one of the city's most recognizable public art spaces, ensuring that her memory will be visible to thousands who cross the bridge daily.

item.title: Fort Walton Beach Lowe's hosts bed-building event for local children

item.content:encoded:
Volunteers are being sought to help construct beds for children in need during a community service event at the Fort Walton Beach Lowe's, according to organizers.

The effort brings together Lowe's, the nonprofit Sleep in Heavenly Peace, and local volunteers to build and donate beds to children in the Fort Walton Beach area who might otherwise go without. Sleep in Heavenly Peace operates across the country with a mission focused on ensuring every child has a safe place to sleep.

The event offers residents a chance to get hands-on with a meaningful project while supporting families facing housing insecurity or financial hardship. No carpentry experience is necessary, and all materials and tools are typically provided by the organizing partners.

Interested volunteers can contact Lowe's or reach out to Sleep in Heavenly Peace for event details and sign-up information.

item.title: Mobile County Schools Earn National Recognition for Attendance Gains
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: The Mobile County Public School System is being recognized nationally for making significant strides in reducing chronic absenteeism, according to a school system news release. Attendance Works, an organization that tracks school attendance patterns across the country, credited MCPSS with "impressive progress" in addressing what has become a…
item.content:encoded:
The Mobile County Public School System is being recognized nationally for making significant strides in reducing chronic absenteeism, according to a school system news release. Attendance Works, an organization that tracks school attendance patterns across the country, credited MCPSS with "impressive progress" in addressing what has become a widespread challenge in American education.

Chronic absenteeism—typically defined as missing 10 percent or more of school days—has been identified by education experts as a critical factor affecting student achievement and long-term outcomes. The recognition suggests Mobile County's efforts to keep students in classrooms are paying off.

The school system did not immediately provide specific attendance figures or detail which programs or initiatives drove the improvement. MCPSS serves more than 60,000 students across Mobile County.
